extracted.intended_audience: attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO and counsel in USPTO disciplinary matters
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order resolving USPTO disciplinary proceedings against a registered practitioner, stating stipulated facts, legal conclusions under the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, and agreed sanctions. Useful for understanding grounds for misconduct findings and typical sanctions/procedures in Office disciplinary matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction for disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over this matter pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicable where a practitioner is engaged in practice before the Office; respondent practiced before the Office in trademark matters. Establishes statutory and regulatory bases the Office relies on to bring and resolve disciplinary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b) — criminal act as professional misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional misconduct for a practitioner to commit a criminal act (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order applies this provision to respondent's convictions for misdemeanor possession of a firearm in a public place and misdemeanor driving under the influence, holding that those convictions constitute misconduct under § 11.804(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1) — public discipline by a state as professional misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Professional misconduct to be publicly disciplined on ethical or professional grounds by any duly constituted authority of a State (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied here because the Supreme Court of California publicly disciplined respondent (one-year stayed suspension subject to probation and other conditions); such state discipline supports a finding of misconduct under the cited regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipulated factual record as basis for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agreement resolves all disciplinary action arising from the stipulated facts set forth in the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office and respondent submit and rely on a joint stipulated factual record (convictions, state discipline, expungements, etc.) as the foundation for legal conclusions and sanctions; factual admissions (acknowledgment of lapses, convictions, expungements) form the operative record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of expunged convictions and disciplinary history in record
rubrics_metrics.description: Stipulated facts include that respondent's 2008 DUI conviction was expunged in October 2016 and the 2021 firearm conviction was expunged in April 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expungement appears in the stipulated factual background and thus is part of the record the Office may consider when assessing sanctions or future matters, though the Order does not state that expungement eliminates misconduct findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating factors for sanctioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors considered in mitigation include respondent's acknowledgment of ethical lapses, genuine contrition, acceptance of responsibility, cooperation with OED's investigation, and limited current practice (two pending trademark applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These mitigating considerations are explicitly noted by the parties and evidently informed the agreed sanction; such factors are relevant when deciding appropriate discipline in USPTO proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreed sanction — public reprimand
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifically orders a public reprimand as the agreed sanction resolving the disciplinary matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication requirements for disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room and shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided notice text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order prescribes where and how the reprimand and summary notice must be published (FOIA Reading Room link provided, Official Gazette notice wording provided); publication is part of the sanction and transparency obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette notice content standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Official Gazette notice must be materially consistent with the supplied 'Notice of Reprimand' text describing the practitioner, the violations (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(b) and § 11.804(h)(1)), the predicate convictions, and the state discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order supplies model language for the Gazette notice, specifying content to identify the practitioner, describe the misconduct, and state that the action results from a settlement agreement under specified statutes and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Future use of disciplinary record (aggravating/rebuttal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement or Final Order prevents the Office from considering the record of this disciplinary proceeding when addressing any further complaint or evidence of the same or similar misconduct and in any future disciplinary proceeding against respondent (i) as an aggravating factor and/or (ii) to rebut any statement or representation by or on respondent's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order preserves the Office's right to treat this record as aggravating evidence or to rebut representations in subsequent matters; settlement does not preclude future disciplinary reliance on these facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of rights to reconsideration and appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent waives all rights to seek reconsideration of the Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56, waives the right to have the Final Order reviewed under 37 C.F.R. § 11.57, and waives the right otherwise to appeal or challenge the Final Order in any manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of the settlement, respondent gives up administrative reconsideration and review rights and any other appeal rights regarding this Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director and respondent shall each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the terms of this Agreement and any Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement terms allocate financial responsibility for costs to each party separately, with no award of costs from one party to the other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirement — certificate of service
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order includes a Certificate of Service certifying that the Final Order was sent to the parties in the manner indicated (via e-mail to listed counsel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documenting service to counsel and including a certificate of service are required procedural steps in the disposition and publication of disciplinary orders.
